details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/render_prompt.sh:618-627 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The shell wrapper clears UNATTENDED_IDENTITY_REINJECT_ENABLED before the Python backend runs even when shell-side identity injection failed, disabling the backend fallback and its richer diagnostics.
  WHY: This leaves users with no identity block when the shell path fails, because IDENTITY_RECALL_INJECTED_FILE is unset but the backend is still invoked with reinjection turned off.
- scripts/render_prompt.sh:92-118 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: identity_reinject_enabled treats whitespace-only UNATTENDED_IDENTITY_REINJECT_ENABLED values as enabled instead of disabled.
  WHY: A whitespace-only env var can silently turn the feature on when the operator intended it off.
- scripts/render_prompt.sh:92-118 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: identity_reinject_enabled reports a generic IDENTITY_REINJECT_PARSE_FAIL instead of a structured reason-specific diagnostic.
  WHY: That limits downstream telemetry and obscures why the flag was rejected.
- scripts/render_prompt.sh:284-391 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The inline Python path can raise uncaught OSError/UnicodeDecodeError from read_text/write_text, producing a raw traceback instead of the script's single-line failure handling.
  WHY: That breaks the stable diagnostic contract and pollutes logs.
- scripts/render_prompt.sh:282-283,453-461 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The global trap handler can overwrite IDENTITY_RECALL_INJECTED_FILE without checking for an existing value, risking cleanup of the wrong file or stale trap state.
  WHY: If the handler is reinstalled or rerun, cleanup may unlink a collateral temp file instead of the intended one.
- scripts/render_prompt.sh:237-283 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The inline Python metadata extraction has no explicit failsafe, so any Python syntax/runtime failure aborts the shell script.
  WHY: A parse failure becomes a hard exit instead of a graceful prompt-rendering failure.
- scripts/render_prompt.sh:280-283 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The /tmp/.${PROMPT_BASENAME}.identity.XXXXXX temp file naming can collide across parallel renderer invocations.
  WHY: Concurrent runs can overwrite or leak identity-injection temp files between processes.
- README.md:1177-1183 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The updated README text describes the shell as "injecting the same block before invoking the Python backend with UNATTENDED_IDENTITY_REINJECT_ENABLED=false" and calls that "byte-identical shell behavior," which is internally contradictory.
  WHY: The wording obscures that the shell performs its own injection and only disables the backend copy to avoid duplication.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "document compaction discipline and add transcript archiving" / update prompt files to reference the sanitized transcript archive naming pattern (.transcripts/<sanitized-run_id>-<sanitized-phase>-<ts>.json)
  expected_change_site: prompts/header.txt, prompts/_prelude_common.txt, prompts/_prelude_common_large.txt, prompts/_prelude_common_xl.txt, and all prompts/mode-*.txt that reference the transcript archive pattern
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  EVIDENCE: README.md and probably_unnecessary_but_read_if_stuck.md were updated to the sanitized pattern, but prompt files under prompts/ still reference .transcripts/<run_id>-<phase>-<ts>.json while scripts/transcript_archive.sh sanitizes both run_id and phase; unattended_system_instructions.md §22 also uses the sanitized pattern.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/render_prompt.sh:621-627 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Both the assembled-prompt path and the exec path unconditionally set UNATTENDED_IDENTITY_REINJECT_ENABLED=false before invoking the Python backend, even when the shell-side identity injection failed.
  WHY: On failure, IDENTITY_RECALL_INJECTED_FILE is never set and the Python backend's own reinjection/fallback logic is disabled, so the rendered output can miss the `<identity-recall>` block entirely.
- Requirement: "document compaction discipline and add transcript archiving" (linked issue #3684, Phase A)
  Expected change site: prompts/header.txt, prompts/_prelude_common.txt, prompts/_prelude_common_large.txt, prompts/_prelude_common_xl.txt, and all prompts/mode-*.txt that reference the transcript archive pattern
  Evidence of absence: The PR updated README.md and probably_unnecessary_but_read_if_stuck.md to reference `.transcripts/<sanitized-run_id>-<sanitized-phase>-<ts>.json`, but 30 prompt files under `prompts/` still reference `.transcripts/<run_id>-<phase>-<ts>.json`.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- scripts/render_prompt.sh:618-627 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The shell wrapper unconditionally clears UNATTENDED_IDENTITY_REINJECT_ENABLED=false before invoking the Python backend, regardless of whether shell-side identity injection succeeded or failed.
  WHY: When shell injection fails, IDENTITY_RECALL_INJECTED_FILE is never set but the backend is still called with reinjection disabled, preventing the Python backend from attempting its own reinjection as a fallback.
- scripts/render_prompt.sh:623-626 | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The inline comment says "the Python renderer will not perform identity injection when UNATTENDED_IDENTITY_REINJECT_ENABLED=false" but that is factually incorrect.
  WHY: The shell clears the variable only to prevent duplicate injection when shell-side reinjection succeeds; the backend would perform injection if called with the flag enabled.
- Requirement: Document transcript archive naming with sanitization
  Expected change site: prompts/header.txt (line 8), prompts/_prelude_common.txt (line 7), and all prompts/mode-*.txt files (line 7 each)
  Evidence of absence: All prompt files still reference `.transcripts/<run_id>-<phase>-<ts>.json` while `scripts/transcript_archive.sh` (lines 78-83) produces `.transcripts/<sanitized-run_id>-<sanitized-phase>-<ts>.json`.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM mistralai_mistral-small-2603 ===
- scripts/render_prompt.sh:92-118 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Whitespace-only strings are accepted as truthy after trimming/lowercasing because the normalized value is allowed by the case statement instead of being rejected explicitly.
  WHY: Mis-setting the boolean env var can silently enable identity-recall injection when the operator intended it off.
- scripts/render_prompt.sh:284-391 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: No exception handling around `source_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")` or `target_path.write_text(updated, encoding="utf-8")`, so OSError and UnicodeDecodeError propagate a full Python traceback.
  WHY: Raw tracebacks violate fail-open diagnostics and can pollute GitHub Actions logs.
- scripts/render_prompt.sh:282-283,453-461 | severity=high | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Global trap handler overwrites IDENTITY_RECALL_INJECTED_FILE without checking if a prior run already set it.
  WHY: The cleanup handler can delete the wrong file or leave a stale handle in traps.
- scripts/render_prompt.sh:624-627 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The wrapper unconditionally clears UNATTENDED_IDENTITY_REINJECT_ENABLED before invoking the Python backend even when identity recall failed on the shell path.
  WHY: A missing canonical prompt file or metadata error leaves IDENTITY_RECALL_INJECTED_FILE unset, yet the backend is still invoked with reinjection disabled, suppressing the fallback attempt and richer diagnostics.
- scripts/render_prompt.sh:92-118 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Parsing emits a generic fail-open `IDENTITY_REINJECT_PARSE_FAIL` to stderr rather than a structured diagnostics line with the concrete reason (`"whitespace"`).
  WHY: This limits downstream telemetry inference.
- scripts/render_prompt.sh:237-283 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The heredoc invokes Python inline without a failsafe, so any Python execution failure (syntax, runtime) produces an abrupt shell exit and halts the script.
  WHY: Lack of inline-script exception handling turns a graceful parse fail into a hard script abort.
- scripts/render_prompt.sh:280-283 | severity=high | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Temporary file location in /tmp/.${PROMPT_BASENAME}.identity.XXXXXX collides with parallel renderer invocations across different prompt files or different shells sharing the same TMPDIR.
  WHY: Race conditions can overwrite or leak identity-injection temp files between unrelated render processes.
=== END FINDINGS FROM mistralai_mistral-small-2603 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===
- scripts/render_prompt.sh:618-627 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The shell wrapper unconditionally clears UNATTENDED_IDENTITY_REINJECT_ENABLED=false before invoking the Python backend, even when shell-side identity injection failed.
  WHY: When shell-side injection fails, the wrapper still invokes the backend with reinjection disabled, so the identity block is omitted instead of falling back to the backend implementation.
- scripts/render_prompt.sh:100-116 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: identity_reinject_enabled treats whitespace-only values as enabled instead of disabled.
  WHY: Setting UNATTENDED_IDENTITY_REINJECT_ENABLED="  " incorrectly enables identity reinjection when it should be treated as false/empty.
- scripts/render_prompt.sh:618-627 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The fail-open behavior on shell identity-injection failure now disables reinjection for downstream consumers instead of allowing the backend to attempt its own path.
  WHY: Any transient condition that breaks the shell-side injection chain results in the identity-recall block being absent from the rendered prompt with no second-chance recovery.
- Requirement: Update prompt files to reference sanitized transcript archive naming pattern (.transcripts/<sanitized-run_id>-<sanitized-phase>-<ts>.json)
  Expected change site: prompts/header.txt, prompts/mode-*.txt, prompts/_prelude_common.txt (and any other prompt files referencing the old pattern)
  Evidence of absence: The transcript archive naming was updated in README.md, probably_unnecessary_but_read_if_stuck.md, and unattended_system_instructions.md §22, but prompt files that document or reference the transcript archive path still use the unsanitized pattern .transcripts/<run_id>-<phase>-<ts>.json.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===
